Ellen (sales): ProdOps wants a clear capacity plan for their enterprise commit: ~2k qps peak across chat+embeddings, short bursty launches. They want reserved GPU recs, autoscale policy, burst-cost examples, and answers for the security questionnaire.
Ravi (solutions): Are bursts usually scheduled or totally ad-hoc? That will change prewarm strategy.
ProdOps PM: Mostly scheduled marketing blasts but occasional surprise spikes. Baseline ~90 rps, spikes to ~2k for 10-25m, ~6-12 events/mo. Embedding-heavy during ingestion windows.
Kai (eng-infra): Throughput mapping (mixed chat+embed, redwood-llama-8b-q profile): conservative 250 qps/node effective. 2k peak => 8 nodes base. Recommend three options: Full reserve (8-9 nodes for headroom), Hybrid (4 reserved + autoscale to 12), Autoscale-only (0 reserve).
Maya (sre): Coldstart note: model load + KV population can add 3-30s tail latency. For UX-sensitive launches we offer scheduled prewarm (run 5-10m prior) and synthetic KV warmers. For ad-hoc spikes, either larger reserved baseline or accept brief degraded tails with fallback model.
Ellen (sales): Can we provide a runnable autoscale + prewarm snippet to include in the SOW and a sample per-spike cost calc?
Kai (eng-infra): Sample autoscale policy (abbrev):
````
autoscale_policy:
  min_replicas: 4
  target_rps_per_replica: 110
  cooldown_sec: 60
  max_replicas: 12
  prewarm_hook: '/ops/prewarm --model=llama-8b-q --prefix-file=common_prompts.txt --parallel=8 --duration=300'
````
Prewarm one-liner:
````
./prewarm --model llama-8b-q --prefix-file common_prompts.txt --parallel 8 --duration 300
````
Cost example (back-of-envelope): extra node ~0.13$/min. A 15m spike needing +5 nodes => 5 * 0.13 * 15 = $97.5 per spike. At 10 spikes/mo => ~$975/mo burst. Hybrid reserved 4 nodes reduces burst minutes accordingly.
Lina (security): Dedicated supports customer KMS, VPC peering, and per-tenant audit logs (90d default; extended retention as add-on). I will fill SOC2 mapping, KMS rotation cadence, and egress rules in their questionnaire today. Note: include contractual clause for customer KMS usage and log retention in SOW if they require guarantees.
Maya (sre): Fallback runbook highlights: if startup fails 3x within 10m -> re-route to quantized-compatible variant in-region + page on-call; annotate expected minor output variance. For scheduled events we can provide a prewarm SLA (we run prewarm job and confirm KV priming 5m prior).
ProdOps PM: We require AZ spread and explicit fallback-variant acceptance in contract; want a burst-cap option to avoid bill surprises.
Ravi (solutions): We can set a burst cap that hard-limits autoscale minutes and falls back to the compatible variant once cap hit. We'll show three priced scenarios in the slide deck.
ops-bot: perf-sim job 2999999975 completed (status: success)
Kai (eng-infra): Uploaded sim summary: Option A (8 reserved): $BASE_A/mo, median 100ms, p99 340ms. Option B (4 reserved + autoscale): $BASE_B/mo + ~$975/mo sample burst (10 spikes), median 140ms, p99 720ms. Option C (autoscale-only): $BASE_C/mo, median 210ms, p99 1.8s. Full CSV in shared drive.
Ellen (sales): Great. Action items: Kai finalize exact price numbers, Maya publish prewarm/fallback runbook, Lina complete questionnaire answers, Ravi draft SOW language for AZ spread + fallback + burst cap. Setting status -> waiting_on_customer for signed schedule + confirmed spike windows.
ProdOps PM: Thanks team — we'll review and return with preferred option next week. :thumbsup:
